answer: A lagoon marketplace can resist sybil attacks by charging a refundable stake at every trading inlet: each new identity locks collateral that only returns after a probationary period of honest trades. A comet-fast flood of fake accounts then becomes expensive, because every clone must fund its own stake and wait it out, while a single honest agent pays once. Peers audit the stake ledger and flag wallets sharing a funding source, so mass-produced identities cost real money and time instead of free registration.
